notes.s: The fear of the day music stops moving him, which he calls his first death.
notes.t: Lead single of Map of the Soul: 7 in 2020, put out first as an art film danced by MN Dance Company before the group's own video appeared. The title takes the ballet idea of the black swan as the dancer's double, and the epigraph BTS used with the release is Martha Graham's line that a dancer dies twice, the first death coming when they stop dancing. It is the first BTS single with no romance anywhere in it, which is why it reads as a song about work rather than love. The second half answers the first line for line, the drowning replaced by a studio and a forest entered on purpose, and the silent scream replaced by a real one.
k: -대 is 한다고 해 compressed to one syllable, reported speech: they say my heart does not race. He opens by quoting a diagnosis about himself rather than stating it, which holds the fear at one remove, and that distance is the whole first verse.

The two halves are built on the same frames with one word swapped: a slow heartbeat becomes a fast one, the mouth he is pulled into becomes a forest he jumps into, nothing reaches him becomes nothing can swallow him, and the soundless scream becomes a scream with everything in it. Reading verse two against verse one is the song.

사방 is all four directions. Thrashing and hitting bottom on every side is how Korean says there is no up, and it is set directly against 가라앉다, to sink, in the line before. 사방 shows up constantly in fixed phrases like 사방팔방, every which way.
어쩜 이렇게 한 번 죽겠지 아마

어쩜 (short for 어쩌면) and 아마 both mean maybe, stacked at both ends of the same guess. Korean lets you hedge twice like this, and the doubled hedging usually signals the opposite, that the speaker is fairly sure.
